definition: EDLUT (Event-Driven LookUp Table) is a computer application for simulating networks of spiking neurons.
details: It was developed in the University of Granada and source code was released under GNU GPL version 3. EDLUT uses event-driven simulation scheme and lookup tables to efficiently simulate medium or large spiking neural networks. This allows this application to simulate detailed biological neuron models and to interface with experimental setups (such as a robotic arm) in real time.

explainer.lead: EDLUT is a simulator for networks of spiking neurons, designed to make medium and large networks practical to run. Its event-driven design and lookup tables can also support detailed biological neuron models and real-time connections to experimental equipment.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a crowd where people only pass messages when something happens, instead of everyone checking in every second. EDLUT works a bit like that: it follows signals between model brain cells only when those signals occur, and uses ready-made tables to avoid repeating calculations. This can help researchers run large simulations quickly enough to connect them to equipment such as a robotic arm.
tiers.practitioner: Use EDLUT when simulating medium or large spiking neural networks, including networks built from detailed biological neuron models. Its event-driven processing and lookup tables are intended to reduce simulation cost, and its real-time capability allows interfacing with experimental setups such as a robotic arm. It is a simulator rather than a general-purpose neural-network training framework; source code was released under GNU GPL version 3.
tiers.paperLevel: EDLUT (Event-Driven LookUp Table) is an event-driven spiking-network simulator: network activity is processed as discrete events, while lookup tables provide an efficient means of evaluating neuron behavior. It is designed for medium or large networks and can retain detailed biological neuron models. Its efficiency also permits real-time interfacing with experimental setups.

explainer.example: A researcher can simulate a detailed spiking neural network that controls a robotic arm. EDLUT processes the network's spike events and uses lookup tables for efficient neuron evaluation, allowing the simulation to interface with the arm in real time.

explainer.intuition: Instead of advancing every neuron through every small time step, EDLUT focuses on moments when spikes occur. Lookup tables then supply neuron responses efficiently, making detailed models less costly to simulate.
howItWorks: Represent the neurons with detailed biological models whose behavior can be accessed through lookup tables.
Advance the simulation according to spike events rather than continuously updating every component.
Use the tables to evaluate neuron behavior efficiently as events are processed.
Simulate the resulting activity across a medium or large spiking neural network.
When required, run efficiently enough to exchange signals with an experimental setup in real time.
explainer.whyItMatters: EDLUT combines efficient large-network simulation with detailed biological neuron models, avoiding a simple choice between scale and biological detail. Real-time operation also lets a simulated network participate in experiments involving physical equipment.
misconceptions: EDLUT is not itself a neuron model; it is an application for simulating networks of neuron models.
Its efficiency does not mean it is restricted to simple neurons; it supports detailed biological models.
It is a spiking-network simulator, not a general machine-learning training algorithm.
